subject.title: [Feature]: Control UI HTTP file upload channel for large attachments (bypass WebSocket payload limit)

question: Should OpenClaw support attachments above the WebSocket request budget through a dedicated authenticated media-staging HTTP API, or make the current budget an explicit Control UI attachment limit?
rationale: The reconnect failure is source-reproducible, but the requested solution establishes a permanent core upload, storage, and security contract that the existing parser work intentionally leaves undecided.

options.title: Support staged uploads
options.body: Approve a media-specific authenticated upload endpoint with opaque references, strict quotas, cleanup, and untrusted-content validation.

options.title: Enforce current ceiling
options.body: Reject oversized attachments before reading or enqueueing them and recover any existing unsendable queued messages.

recommendation.title: Support staged uploads
recommendation.body: Approve a media-specific authenticated upload endpoint with opaque references, strict quotas, cleanup, and untrusted-content validation.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history provides the strongest connection across both the Control UI send/retry behavior and gateway payload limit.
